title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Working Out the Price of a Prepaid Hour Block
content:
## The clause

The price of a block of prepaid hours is worked out from the size of the block the account's own drawing
record calls for, the rate that block is sold at, the discount the account's settlement record carries
and any office release charge the purchase attracts. The hours drawn are read over the last 12 months.
The prepaid hours standing are the hours of every block bought within the tier's expiry period less the
hours drawn over the window read, never below nil, and the shortfall is the hours drawn over that window
less the prepaid hours standing, never below nil. A block of prepaid hours is sold as a single one of
the tier's minimum purchase multiples, that is 1 multiple. The hours sold are the multiples sold
multiplied by the tier's minimum purchase. The whole block is priced at the tier's block hour rate. No
discount comes off for the account's settlement record. No office release charge is added. The open
position is everything invoiced on the program over its whole life less every payment received on it
over its whole life, without any window. The headroom is the credit ceiling standing on the rate program
less the open position, and the excess is the block price less that headroom, never below nil. The price
is the block price less the discount, which is worked out on the block price alone and never on the
price after the office release charge is added, with the office release charge added afterwards, and
only the total is rounded, to the nearest cent, half up.

The minimum purchase, the expiry period and the block hour rate are the figures published for the
program the account holds under the Demand Service Rate Programs; the credit ceiling is the one standing
on the rate program.

## Worked through on a hypothetical account

A rate program whose minimum purchase is 40 hours and whose block hour rate is 132 US dollars an hour
carries a credit ceiling of 25000 US dollars, 10000 US dollars invoiced over the life of the program and
8000 US dollars received on it, so the open position is 2000 US dollars and the headroom 23000 US
dollars. One multiple is sold, so the hours sold are 40 and the block price is 40 hours multiplied by
132 US dollars, which is 5280 US dollars. No discount comes off. The excess is the block price less the
headroom, and 5280 US dollars is below 23000 US dollars, so the excess is nil and no office release
charge is added. Rounded to the nearest cent, half up, the price is 5280.00 US dollars.
